question: Nitin bought some pencils at the rate of ₹180 a dozen. He sold them for ₹17 each. His profit percentage is ______%. (Round off to two decimal places.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost price of 1 pencil = ₹180 ÷ 12 = ₹15

Selling price of 1 pencil = ₹17

Profit on 1 pencil = ₹17 − ₹15 = ₹2

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (2 ÷ 15) × 100 = 13.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 13.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price of a dozen (12 pencils) = ₹180

Selling price of 1 pencil = ₹17

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) of 1 unit = Total CP ÷ Quantity

Profit = Selling Price (SP) − Cost Price (CP)

Profit Percentage = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 CP = ₹15
 
 
 SP = ₹17

 

 

 + ₹2 (Profit)
 
 Profit % = (2 ÷ 15) × 100 = 13.33%

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of 1 pencil = 180 ÷ 12 = ₹15

⇒ Profit earned on 1 pencil = 17 − 15 = ₹2

⇒ Profit % = (2 ÷ 15) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 200 ÷ 15 = 40 ÷ 3 = 13.333... %

⇒ Rounding off to two decimal places, Profit % ≈ 13.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 13.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When the cost price (CP) is greater than the selling price (SP), a loss is incurred. Loss = CP − SP. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is an allowance given by the seller to the buyer on the marked price of the goods. SP = MP − Discount. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer claims to sell goods at cost price but uses false weights, he makes a profit. Profit % = (Error ÷ True Weight − Error) × 100.
